pattern.title: Races and Circular Tracks
pattern.description: Races, head starts and motion on circular tracks.

questions.questionText: A runs 400 m in 20 seconds and B runs 400 m in 25 seconds. What start should A give B in a 400 m race for a dead heat?
questions.explanation: B covers 400 m in 25 s, so in 20 s he covers 320 m. A must give B a start of 400 - 320 = 80 m.
questions.shortcut: B must run only the distance he can cover in A's time.

questions.questionText: A runs 100 m in 20 seconds and B runs 100 m in 25 seconds. What start should A give B in a 100 m race for a dead heat?
questions.explanation: B covers 100 m in 25 s, so in 20 s he covers 80 m. A must give B a start of 100 - 80 = 20 m.
questions.shortcut: B must run only the distance he can cover in A's time.

questions.questionText: The speeds of A and B are in the ratio 3:2. In a race of 300 m, how many metres has B run when A finishes?
questions.explanation: Distances in equal time are in the speed ratio. B runs 300 x 2/3 = 200 m.
questions.shortcut: In the same time, distance is proportional to speed.

questions.questionText: A is 3/2 times as fast as B. By how many metres does A beat B in a race of 300 m?
questions.explanation: When A runs 300, B runs 300 x 2/3 = 200. A beats B by 300 - 200 = 100 m.
questions.shortcut: Beating distance = race length x (a - b)/a.

questions.questionText: A can give B a start such that A runs 10 units while B runs 9 units, and B can give C a start such that B runs 5 units while C runs 4 units, in the same time. What start can A give C in a 1000 m race for a dead heat?
questions.explanation: A : B = 10:9 and B : C = 5:4, so A : C = 50:36. C runs 1000 x 36/50 = 720 m while A runs 1000. Start = 280 m.
questions.shortcut: Multiply the two speed ratios to get A : C, then find C's distance in the same time.

questions.questionText: A runs 4/3 times as fast as B. In a race of 160 m, A gives B a start of 50 m. Who wins, and by how many metres?

questions.questionText: Two runners start from the same point on a circular track 1200 m long and run in opposite directions at 2 m/s and 4 m/s. After how many seconds do they first meet?
questions.explanation: They approach each other at 2 + 4 = 6 m/s and must cover 1200 m together. Time = 1200/6 = 200 seconds.
questions.shortcut: Opposite directions: relative speed = sum; distance = one lap.

questions.shortcut: Same direction: relative speed = difference; the faster must gain one lap.

questions.questionText: In a 500 m race A beats B by 20 m and B beats C by 20 m. By how many metres does A beat C in the same race?
